title: FedLTLib: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Federated Long-Tail Learning
abstract: arXiv:2609.15625v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Driven by the escalating demand for privacy-preserving computing, Federated Learning (FL) has witnessed remarkable progress, becoming a cornerstone technology for bridging distributed data silos in mobile edge networks. However, in real-world mobile computing environments, data is generated by heterogeneous mobile devices with varying user behaviors, leading to a significant Long-Tail Distribution. Unlike idealized balanced datasets, data in the wild manifests an acute imbalance where a minority of head classes dominate the sample space while a vast number of tail classes, often representing rare but critical edge-case events, are extremely scarce. translated_title: FedLTLib：一个面向联邦长尾学习的综合基准
translated_abstract: 在隐私保护计算需求不断升级的驱动下，联邦学习（FL）取得了显著进展，成为连接移动边缘网络中分布式数据孤岛的基石技术。然而，在真实世界的移动计算环境中，数据由具有不同用户行为的异构移动设备生成，导致显著的长尾分布。与理想化的均衡数据集不同，现实中的数据表现出严重的不平衡：少数头部类别主导样本空间，而大量的尾部类别（通常代表罕见但关键的边缘情况事件）则极为稀缺。这种数据异构性被论文正式表征为“双重异构性”，即全局类别不平衡与本地统计偏斜的叠加，会导致尾部类别的性能严重恶化，从而催生了联邦长尾学习这一重要研究方向。
tldr: 本文提出了FedLTLib，一个面向联邦长尾学习的综合基准，正式刻画了由全局类别不平衡与本地统计偏斜叠加而成的“双重异构性”问题。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces FedLTLib, a comprehensive benchmark for federated long-tail learning, formally characterizing the "Double Heterogeneity" problem arising from the superposition of global class imbalance and local statistical skew.
